evidence: Thin ﬁlms of cobalt oxides were deposited in a commercial F-120 Sat reactor (ASM Microchemistry Ltd.) using ozone and CoCp 2 (cobaltocene) as precursors. CoCp2 was used at room temperature in a bubbler with nitrogen as the carrier gas. The ozone was generated by feeding O 2 (99.999% AGA) into an OT-020 ozone generator (Ozone Technology), giving an ozone concentration of 15 vol.-% according to speciﬁcations. An ozone ﬂow of approx. 500 cm 3 min−1 was used during the ozone pulses. During all depositions, a background pressure of approx. 3.5 mbar was obtained by applying a N2 carrier gas ﬂow of 300 cm3 min−1. The process was evaluated for possible CVD-type growth by performing experiments under the speciﬁed conditions for CoCp 2 sublimation while not pulsing ozone.
